_comment: Fundraising proposal for HSR Capital (Karson Jones). From the Oct 19 2026 strategy call with Matt, plus HSR's Investor Day 2026 deck and three note summaries (Camas Woods, Kozy Manor, Oslund Acres). One profile (Karson's) in scope, with partner Dustin's profile as the scale option. Note rates deliberately kept out of the deck; it will be forwarded to the partners.

cards.label: THE GOAL
cards.text: Grow HSR’s investor base beyond one person’s network ahead of a $50M+ raise year: the Washington pipeline plus $15–20M for Generation Homes’ Idaho expansion, with capital needed by the end of Q2 2027. New relationships take time, so they need to start in Q1. Minimum check $200K; most land between $200K and $700K.

cards.label: THE PLAN
cards.text: Karson’s LinkedIn profile, run end to end by ThinkFISH in his voice, building new relationships with accredited real estate investors in the Pacific Northwest, Idaho and the coastal markets looking for growth-market exposure. Relationship-first, never a solicitation of the offering. Every meeting pre-qualified and approved by you.

cards.label: THE INVESTMENT
cards.text: $3,000 per month for Karson’s profile, or $3,500 with Dustin’s profile added. Flat, on a four-month term. No setup fee, no success fee, no commission, no points on capital raised, no transaction involvement. A team behind your capital raiser instead of a second hire.

band.label: WHAT TO EXPECT
band.text: Outreach live within two weeks of kickoff. First qualified investor conversations in weeks three and four, building to a steady 1–2 qualified meetings per week from Karson’s profile from month two, more once a second profile is added. Weekly reporting throughout. One honest note for the partners: these are new relationships, not friends and family, so first meeting to signed note takes longer than your warm network does. Plan on months, not weeks. That is why we’d start in January for a Q2 close, and we’d rather you hear it from us now.

gap.narrative: HSR has done the hard part: $40M of investor capital, an investor who started with $1M in 2020 and is now at $5M, notes that roll like season tickets, and $25M of this year’s $30M raised by one person. The constraint is structural, not the offering. Because the notes can’t be generally solicited, every investor has to come through a relationship, and one person’s 3,500 connections, mutuals and tee times have a ceiling. Next year needs around $50M.
gap.principle: Private capital is a relationship game at volume. Inside 506 rules, the variable you control is how many new, qualified relationships with accredited real estate investors start every week, long before the next note needs to be filled.
rows: One capital raiser working a warm network that’s close to tapped: LinkedIn mutuals, referrals and country-club tee times, with a month-or-two slump between hot streaks.
Washington plus $15–20M for Idaho puts next year at around $50M, all raised by one person. Idaho is a new market, and HSR has no investor network there yet.
Karson carries every raise alone, and the fallback on the table is relocating to Boise for three or four months to build an Idaho network one country club at a time.
About $15M rolls off mid-to-late Q1. It may all recycle, or 10–20% may not. By the time the gap is known, it’s too late to start the new relationships needed to fill it.

segments.name: PNW Real Estate & Land Investors
segments.why: Accredited individuals and family offices in Portland, Vancouver and Seattle with private real estate or land history. Close enough to walk the sites, and to golf.

segments.name: IDAHO  ·  Treasure Valley Capital
segments.why: Boise-area investors, operators and family offices local to Generation Homes’ expansion. Built remotely so Karson flies in for meetings instead of moving there.

segments.name: Coastal Capital Seeking Growth Markets
segments.why: California, New York and Florida investors priced out of their home markets and allocating to growth regions where entry-level housing is undersupplied.

segments.name: Private Credit & Income Allocators
segments.why: Investors who prefer fixed-income, debt-style real estate positions to equity, write $200K–$1M checks and roll capital from deal to deal.

segments.name: Builders, Lenders & RE Operators
segments.why: Retired homebuilders, lenders and real estate executives who already understand entitlement, horizontal and vertical risk, and need little diligence.

icp.note: These segments are our starting point. A more complete outline of investor targets, including check sizes, geographies and exclusions, will be planned with you during onboarding.

architecture.title: One Raiser Today, Two Profiles to Scale
architecture.subtitle: HOW THE CAMPAIGN GROWS WITH THE RAISE

cards.label: KARSON  ·  CORE CAMPAIGN
cards.text: Karson’s profile carries the core campaign: Pacific Northwest real estate investors for the Washington pipeline, plus the first Idaho and coastal segments. 3,500 connections and an investment background give relationship-first outreach credibility. Every meeting lands on his calendar, already briefed.

cards.label: DUSTIN  ·  WHEN YOU SCALE
cards.text: Adding Dustin’s profile, with roughly 9,000 connections, is the fastest way to add volume, for $500 more a month, for example by pointing it at Idaho and Treasure Valley capital for the Generation Homes expansion. Its own audience, scripts and scorecard. Meetings can still route to Karson, so the partners’ time isn’t spent prospecting.

band.label: WHY START WITH ONE
band.text: Starting on Karson’s profile proves the targeting and the meeting quality on real numbers before the partners commit a second account. The engine is shared either way: one account manager, one CRM, one weekly report. The profile-to-market mapping above is our starting assumption from the call; we’ll confirm it with you in onboarding.

cards.label: OUTREACH VOLUME
cards.text: 800 InMails and 800 connection invites every month from Karson’s profile, once fully warmed up. Every touch scored and hand-reviewed before it goes out.

cards.label: QUALIFIED MEETINGS
cards.unit: per week at steady state (month 2 onward)
cards.text: Our conservative range for one profile once calibrated; real estate audiences often run higher. Add Dustin’s profile and the range moves with it.

cards.label: TIME TO FIRST MEETINGS
cards.unit: weeks from kickoff to first booked calls
cards.text: Weeks one and two are setup: ICP, audiences, scripts, profile warm-up. Live outreach starts in week three, and the first replies and bookings follow within days.

band.label: WHAT “QUALIFIED” MEANS, AND THE HONEST TIMELINE
band.text: A qualified meeting is an accredited individual, family office or fund with a history of similar real estate investments, who passed scoring and human review, completed the self-qualification form on booking, and whose briefing you approved. New relationships close slower than friends and family: plan on months from first meeting to signed note. Start four to six months before the capital is needed, and we’d rather you hear that from us now.

columns.label: WEEKS 3-4  ·  LATE JAN
columns.title: First Live Outreach
bullets: A/B tests by segment and region

columns.label: MONTHS 3-4  ·  MAR-APR
columns.title: Prove-Out & Scale
bullets: Idaho pipeline ahead of the raise

band.label: THE APRIL DECISION
band.text: By the end of the four-month term you’ll have real numbers on audience quality, meeting quality and notes placed, plus a live investor pipeline going into the Q2 close and the Idaho raise. That is the decision point: continue, add Dustin’s profile, or stop. The partners decide on data, not on faith.

cards.label: 1  ·  REVIEW
cards.text: Karson, take this to the partners and send us the questions that come back. In December or January, Matt and Ben Padnos, our CEO, will join a short meeting with the partners to walk through the process, compliance and the numbers directly.

cards.label: 2  ·  SIGN & KICK OFF
cards.text: We send the services agreement the same day you say yes. Onboarding starts that week: one 60-minute interview with Karson, and we connect his LinkedIn profile, no passwords required. Setup in December puts outreach live in early January.

cards.label: 3  ·  FIRST MEETINGS
cards.text: Karson’s profile is live within two weeks of kickoff. The first qualified investor conversations land in weeks three and four, then build to a steady weekly rhythm through February and March, ahead of the Q2 close and the Idaho raise.

band.label: WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU
band.text: Connect Karson’s LinkedIn account to our system (no passwords or login credentials required). Share the Investor Day deck, a current executive summary and any lists of past contacts. One 60-minute onboarding interview. A Calendly link, and a do-not-contact list covering your existing investors and anyone we should avoid. That’s it. We handle the rest.

deliverables.text: 800 InMails and 800 connection invites every month from Karson’s profile, in his voice, once fully warmed up. Every InMail credit in your Sales Navigator plan gets used.
